claims.statement: EUDR begins applying to large and medium enterprises on 30 December 2026 and most micro and small enterprises on 30 June 2027, creating current paid preparation and supplier-data work.
2025 simplifications reduced obligations for some downstream actors, so the initial customer must be an operator with primary due-diligence responsibility rather than a generic trader.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Responsible sourcing, procurement or compliance head at an EUDR operator
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: The service normalizes messy plot files and validates geometry before statement preparation; generic ESG tools may not handle supplier remediation.
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: The prospective business would own operator service contracts; operators retain supplier relationships and regulatory responsibility.
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Commodity consultants and testing/certification partners refer operators.

fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Analyst effort depends on supplier file quality; assumed 10-40 minutes per plot batch.
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Geospatial specialist, legal review, security and insurance estimated at 20,000 PLN monthly.
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Setup plus per-supplier or per-plot validation usage.
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Geospatial compute, analyst remediation and supplier support.

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Traceability platforms will bundle geometry checks; compete on API-neutral normalization and remediation turnaround.
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Operator pays to correct and validate supplier geolocation evidence before a due-diligence submission or shipment release.
commercial_mechanics.payer: EUDR operator importing or placing relevant commodities on the EU market
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Supplier uploads invalid plot geometry or an EUDR readiness deadline approaches.
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Each new plot, supplier, shipment cohort or annual supplier refresh.

contrary_evidence: Application was delayed and obligations simplified, weakening near-term urgency for some firms.
Full traceability suites may include normalization.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Unknown; proposed operator contracts and supplier data-rights agreements are unsigned.
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Process customer-uploaded files without persistent supplier rights and integrate with multiple traceability platforms.
critical_control_point.current_owner: Operators and upstream suppliers control plot and sourcing data; the EU controls its information system.
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: The prospective business would own operator service contracts; operators retain supplier relationships and regulatory responsibility.
critical_control_point.duration: Unknown until data-processing contracts are signed.
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: No current rights to operator or supplier geolocation data.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: The founder would control normalization software; operators control submission and supplier access.
critical_control_point.subject: Supplier plot-geometry normalization workflow

economics.acquisition_route: Offer paid batch validation for coffee, cocoa, wood or rubber operators, then integrate with traceability vendors.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 100 operators at 70,000 PLN annual revenue yields 7M PLN; at 20% owner earnings and 4x value, a 70% stake can exceed 5M PLN in years 7-10. Supplier remediation intensity is unknown.
economics.founder_time: 20 hours weekly; hire geospatial contractor before production commitments.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Usage revenue less compute, analyst remediation and supplier support; target 68%.
economics.payback: Avoiding one blocked shipment or weeks of supplier cleanup should cover a 10,000-30,000 PLN engagement; must be verified.
economics.pricing: 8,000-25,000 PLN setup plus 2-10 PLN per validated plot or supplier-batch minimums.
economics.retention_or_repeat: New sourcing plots and supplier changes generate repeat validations.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Permissioned geometry-error corpus and supplier remediation playbooks.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Operator pays per validated batch before due-diligence or shipment release.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Invalid supplier geometry or approaching application date.

founder_fit: Can begin with narrow paid batches
EU regulatory context is accessible from Poland
risks: Supplier data quality may make margins labor-heavy
Traceability incumbents may bundle the function

structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: proposed pre submission geometry validation gate
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: upstream suppliers providing lawful plot data

thesis: Control the narrow pre-submission geometry gate where operators already incur supplier-cleanup costs, without attempting a full traceability suite.
title: EUDR Geolocation Normalizer
